newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown says will move quickly on budget.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown says will move quickly on budget.

text.p: Gordon Brown, Britain's opposition Labour Party's finance spokesman, said on Thursday he would move very quickly on the first budget.
"We fully intend to keep all our promises and will move very quickly on a budget," he told ITN.
Brown is expected to be named British finance minister on Friday if predictions showing a landslide Labour victory are correct.
He said a Labour government would deliver the first budget within two months and stick to the commitments made during the election campaign.

"I have said the budget will be within two months. It is a budget to equip this country for the future. I made four commitments -- one on the basic and top rate of tax, one on cutting VAT on fuel, which we will do in the first budget so it will be in by the winter fuel bills for pensioners."
Brown said a Labour government would not extend VAT to items like food, children's clothes, books and newspapers.
"These are the commitments we made and we fully intend to keep them. The important thing is building a new trust between the government and the people.
"I think it makes a change to have a government which is on the side of the people," Brown told ITN.
